findings.summary: Only the first page of the rules/branches reply is read
findings.evidence: From reading the code, `gh api <path>` is called without `--paginate`. The host splits this reply into pages (30 rules per page by default, an estimate from GitHub's API docs), so a branch with more rules than that could show a rule as not in force. This is unlikely for these two branches.

summary: I recommend accepting this change. It adds `host_rules` to athena-core, a read-only check. For `athena/records` and `main` it reads `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}` with a plain `gh api <path>` request, which is a GET. It reports force-push forbidden, deletion forbidden and up-to-date required as in force, not in force or unknown. A failed call or an unreadable reply gives unknown for every rule on that branch, and the other branch still gets its own result. The module doc, the report text, the CHANGELOG and the design doc all say the check sees rulesets only, not classic branch protection. The CHANGELOG cites §3 and §10. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core host_rules`: all 5 new tests passed. I confirmed that `GhCli` passes the arguments through unchanged, so the real `gh` call adds no method override either. The workspace fmt, clippy and test checks come from Athena's records for this tree, and all passed. Only the five planned files changed. One small risk: a reply that runs past one page could be cut short (see findings). Nothing is wired into a command yet, as the brief intends.
